questions.q: How is Oracle Fusion Cloud typically accessed?
options: Entirely through a web browser, at a URL specific to the customer's environment
Through a dedicated desktop application that must be installed
Only through a mobile app
Through a direct database connection
questions.explain: Fusion Cloud is accessed entirely through a browser, at a URL specific to each environment (production and non-production each have their own address).

questions.q: Why might two different employees see noticeably different home pages after signing into the same Oracle Fusion environment?
options: Because each employee uses a different web browser
Because their assigned security roles differ, determining what work areas and data they can see
Because the home page is randomized for each login
Because only one home page design exists per company
questions.explain: A user's security roles determine which work areas, menus, and data they see — two users can have very different home pages based on their roles.

options: A full-page detailed report
A type of security role
A small, interactive widget on the home page surfacing a glanceable, role-relevant summary
The name of Oracle's mobile app
questions.explain: Infolets are small widgets giving a quick summary — for example, an AP clerk might see one showing invoices awaiting approval — without opening a full report.

questions.q: What is the 'springboard' on the Oracle Fusion home page?
options: The notifications bell in the global header
The quarterly update readiness document
A security setting controlling password complexity
The grid of icons on the home page that shortcut into a user's accessible work areas
questions.explain: The springboard is the grid of work-area shortcut icons on the home page, giving a user one-click access to their most frequent starting points.

questions.q: What design philosophy does this lesson say Oracle's home page is built around?
options: Letting a user know within seconds of logging in what needs their attention, without digging through menus first
Requiring users to open a report before seeing anything important
Hiding all information until the user searches for it
Showing identical information to every user regardless of role
questions.explain: Oracle designed the home page around glanceable information — infolets and springboard shortcuts exist specifically so users see what matters immediately upon signing in.
